checks.name: a5-scheduler-checked-before-the-owner-map
checks.summary: A5 MEASURED. internal/api/CombinedAuthenticator gains exactly one field, SchedulerIdentity string. Authenticate's order is unchanged where it matters and the new branch sits in exactly one place: (1) the runner-session header branch, BYTE-UNCHANGED (verified by `git diff` over auth.go, which touches only the struct declaration and the block between parseIAPEmail and the OwnerEmails lookup); (2) parseIAPEmail; (3) NEW -- IdentityConfigurationError() refuses an overlap between SchedulerIdentity and OwnerEmails (the same predicate the start-time constructor calls, so the two refusals are one rule), then application.LoopCaller(email) is returned when the trimmed lowercased SchedulerIdentity equals the asserted email; (4) the existing OwnerEmails lookup and RoleOwner return, unchanged. Checking BEFORE the owner map is load-bearing, not stylistic: an identity that resolved as owner first would silently acquire every owner-only route. ASSERTED, executed: the same authenticator resolves the scheduler address to RoleScheduler with the asserted email as Subject and an empty RunnerID, resolves the allowlisted owner to RoleOwner, refuses a stranger, folds case on both sides (an upper-case assertion of the scheduler address still resolves, and the Subject is the normalised lowercase form, which is what makes it usable as a domain ActorID), and -- with the field left empty -- behaves exactly as it did at a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab: the scheduler's own address is simply not an owner and is refused. Verdict: '--- PASS: TestCombinedAuthenticatorResolvesTheSchedulerBeforeTheOwnerMap'.

checks.name: a5-a6-an-identity-configured-as-both-is-refused
checks.summary: A5's and A6's REFUSAL PROOF, executed. An email present in BOTH OwnerEmails and SchedulerIdentity makes Authenticate return an ERROR naming the misconfiguration -- 'misconfigured identity: the scheduler identity is also an owner email; an asserted identity must have exactly one role' -- and never a Caller: the test asserts, for the overlapping address AND for the separate owner address AND for a stranger, that err is non-nil, that the returned Caller is the zero value, and that the message contains 'scheduler identity is also an owner email'. The refusal is deliberately UNCONDITIONAL on the asserted identity rather than scoped to the overlapping one, because a deployment in that state has no defensible answer for any IAP caller; it is not resolved by precedence, because a single asserted email must produce exactly one role or an error. The rule itself lives in ONE place, CombinedAuthenticator.IdentityConfigurationError, which the start-time constructor also calls, and a test asserts the two error strings are byte-equal so they cannot drift. Case folding and padding do not let the overlap slip through: SchedulerIdentity '  RECONCILER@Example.IAM.gserviceaccount.COM  ' against an OwnerEmails entry of the lowercase form is refused too. Verdict: '--- PASS: TestCombinedAuthenticatorRefusesAnIdentityConfiguredAsBothSchedulerAndOwner'.

checks.name: a6-the-start-time-refusal-exists-and-is-proven-by-execution
checks.summary: A6's start-time half, MET, and the route to it is recorded because this item was first reported UNMET. THE ORIGINAL ESCALATION: A6 asks for three things -- (i) the process must FAIL TO START when RECONCILE_IDENTITY is also in OWNER_EMAILS, naming the conflict; (ii) add no environment variable and change nothing else in cmd/control-plane/main.go; (iii) assert the refusal by unit-testing the authenticator, since cmd/control-plane has no test package. Satisfying (i) inside cmd/control-plane means an added guard, which (ii) forbids and which (iii) implies cannot be tested, and an untested guard is not a guard. THE RULING: the conflict dissolves if the predicate does not live in cmd/control-plane. THE REPAIR, as ruled: internal/api gains NewCombinedAuthenticator(runnerService, ownerEmails, schedulerIdentity) (CombinedAuthenticator, error), the same (T, error) shape NewJSONOperatorRecorder established, and CombinedAuthenticator.IdentityConfigurationError is the SINGLE source of truth for the rule -- both the constructor and Authenticate call it, so the start-time and request-time refusals cannot drift apart or disagree on the message, which is asserted by comparing the two error strings for equality. cmd/control-plane/main.go:191-195 now reads `combined, err := api.NewCombinedAuthenticator(runnerEnrollment, owners, strings.ToLower(reconcileIdentity))` followed by `if err != nil { return err }`, so run() returns BEFORE ListenAndServe. All three conditions now hold at once: (i) the process fails to start; (ii) no environment variable was added and the diff is one call plus one error return, the same shape as the line it replaced; (iii) the logic is unit-tested in internal/api and the untested part is one call site. REFUSAL PROOF, executed: TestNewCombinedAuthenticatorRefusesAnIdentityConfiguredAsBothSchedulerAndOwner passes for three configurations -- the scheduler identity as the only owner, as one of several owners, and overlapping only after case-folding and trimming -- and for each it asserts the error names the conflict, that the returned CombinedAuthenticator is the ZERO value (so a caller that ignored the error cannot hold a working authenticator), and that Authenticate's refusal message is byte-equal to the constructor's. TestNewCombinedAuthenticatorAcceptsADistinctSchedulerIdentity is the positive control: a distinct scheduler identity constructs and resolves both roles, and an ABSENT scheduler identity constructs too, because the field is opt-in. Verdicts: '--- PASS: TestNewCombinedAuthenticatorRefusesAnIdentityConfiguredAsBothSchedulerAndOwner' with all three subtests passing, and '--- PASS: TestNewCombinedAuthenticatorAcceptsADistinctSchedulerIdentity'. The request-boundary refusal is KEPT as defence in depth, because every test in this repository builds a CombinedAuthenticator as a composite literal and so bypasses the constructor entirely.

checks.name: a6-the-start-time-refusal-executed-against-the-real-binary
argv: env -i INSTALLATION_ID=install GCP_PROJECT_ID=v2086-local OWNER_EMAILS=owner@example.com,reconciler@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com OWNER_ORIGINS=https://console.example RECONCILE_IDENTITY=reconciler@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:8 AGENTIC_LOOP_ALLOW_FIRESTORE_EMULATOR=1 PORT=18086 ./control-plane; echo EXIT_STATUS=$?
checks.summary: A6 asserted BY EXECUTION rather than by reading, as instructed. The cmd/control-plane binary was built OUT OF TREE (into the session scratchpad, so no artefact entered the worktree and `git status --porcelain` stayed clean) and run twice with a deliberately conflicting configuration and then a valid one. Everything is local: no Google Cloud resource was touched. run() reaches the Firestore constructor BEFORE the authenticator, so both runs set FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:8 with AGENTIC_LOOP_ALLOW_FIRESTORE_EMULATOR=1 and APP_ENV unset; the Firestore client is constructed lazily and dials nothing, which is why the authenticator is reached at all. (1) CONFLICTING -- OWNER_EMAILS=owner@example.com,reconciler@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com with RECONCILE_IDENTITY=reconciler@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com. VERBATIM stderr, the single line the process printed: 'control-plane: misconfigured identity: the scheduler identity is also an owner email; an asserted identity must have exactly one role'. EXIT_STATUS=1. Nothing listened on the port. So the process FAILS TO START and NAMES THE CONFLICT, at the only moment an operator is positioned to fix it, instead of starting and then presenting as an authentication outage. (2) NON-CONFLICTING -- the same environment with OWNER_EMAILS=owner@example.com only. The process STARTED: GET http://127.0.0.1:18086/healthz returned '{"schema_version":"v1","status":"ok"}' on the first poll of a bounded 100-iteration poll loop (no fixed sleep), stderr was EMPTY, and SIGTERM shut it down through the existing graceful path with exit status 0.
